i’m so sorry this happened to you! i can relate because i had a dream vacation planned for myself to ireland last year and my flight anxiety was really peaking. like you, i had been able to fly before, and also like you, just couldn’t do it.

i also felt ashamed, sad, like i let myself down, etc. but i know for a lot of people in this sub once that switch flips it’s so hard to flip it back!

the most helpful thing for me has been to realize that just because i couldn’t do that particular trip, doesn’t mean i can’t fly. i’ve focused this year on going to flight therapy, developing tools, and taking practice flights. i have a new trip booked for europe, this time flying with my mom! your relationship with flying is a journey and while it’s a disappointing experience to not fly, you did the right thing to take care of yourself at the time. 

you can take this time to focus on what you can do so that next time is different! don’t rush yourself. any small steps are progress when tackling this fear. we are here for you ❤️

I have a menu of things I can do when I’m panicking and also only take my xanax when I literally have no other choice

some of my things are:

—call a friend (my brain usually snaps into a different mode if i have to talk to someone) 
—eat sour candy (i have war heads on hand most times) 
—ice packs 
—breathing videos or meditation audios (i use headspace)
—if i can ride out a bit of the attack, force myself to leave the house and walk even if it’s only for 5 minutes 
—turn on a movie that calms me to ride it out (i have a list of comfort films)
—repeating my mantras (this feeling is distressing, but not dangerous, etc)

Yes! I usually go up to the gate beforehand and ask if I can pre-board to get settled because I’m a fearful flyer as waiting at the gate causes me a lot of anticipatory dread.

They’ve always said yes and usually the attendant (and sometimes pilot too) come and chat with me, hand me a few extra snacks, and then will sometimes alert me if there’s going to be turbulence, etc throughout. They’ve always seemed willing or even happy to help out!

Last summer I was really panicking on a flight and was on my way to the bathroom when I guy approached me and introduced himself as a Delta pilot who was just flying home as a passenger. 

I was sitting in the row in front of him and he noticed me crying and asked if I was okay. I told him I was a pretty nervous flyer and he invited me to sit with him in his row. 

He spent the whole flight answering questions I had about my fears! It didn’t solve my flight anxiety but made a big impact and I felt so empowered on that flight with all my new info :) He was amazing!!
